#{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("fredr", "tidyverse"))


#{r cars}
# Load them into the R session (do this every time you start R):
library(fredr)     # lets us query FRED with fredr()
library(tidyverse) # gives us ggplot2, dplyr, readr, etc.



#{r API}
fredr_set_key("aba39be8447ebff96c9230ec5ae6b007")


#{r cars}
library(ggplot2)
library(fredr)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)

# brand colours
col_orange <- "#E87722"
col_text   <- "#0C233C"
col_gray   <- "gray95"

# reusable grey-panel theme
theme_fred <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
    theme(
      plot.background      = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),    # white overall background
      panel.background     = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),    # white plotting area
      panel.grid.major.x   = element_line(color = "gray80", size = 0.5),  # vertical gridlines
      panel.grid.major.y   = element_line(color = "gray80", size = 0.5),  # horizontal gridlines ← ADD THIS
      panel.grid.minor     = element_blank(),                              # clean look
      axis.text            = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
      axis.title           = element_text(size = 13),
      plot.title           = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle        = element_text(size = 13, face = "plain"),
      plot.caption         = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.x          = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.margin          = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
    )
}

# helper to build caption text
fred_caption <- function(series_id) {
  paste0("Source: FRED (Series: ", series_id, ")")
}




#{r Balance Sheet}
# Pull Fed balance-sheet data for calendar year 2025
walcl <- fredr(
  series_id         = "WALCL",          # FRED code for total assets of the Fed
  observation_start = as.Date("2024-07-01"),
  observation_end   = as.Date("2025-12-31")
)

# Peek at the first few rows
head(walcl)


#{r PlotBSheet}
ggplot(walcl, aes(x = date, y = value / 1e3)) +   # scale to billions
  geom_line(color = col_orange, size = 1) +
  labs(
    title    = "Federal Reserve Balance Sheet",
    subtitle = "Levels, 2025",
    x        = NULL,                         # cleaner x-label
    y        = "Billions of U.S. Dollars",
    caption  = fred_caption("WALCL")         # ✅ add the citation here
  ) +
  theme_fred()   

#{r T10Y2Y}
# Fetch the ready-made 2s10s spread series
t10y2y <- fredr(
  series_id         = "T10Y2Y",
  observation_start = as.Date("2017-01-01"),
  observation_end   = as.Date("2025-12-31")
)


#{r Drates}
# 3 ── (Optional) recession shading for 2020 COVID downturn  
recess_shade <- data.frame(
  start = as.Date("2020-02-01"),   # NBER recession: Feb-2020
  end   = as.Date("2020-04-30")    #             …  Apr-2020
)


#{r T10Y2Y}
ggplot(t10y2y, aes(date, value)) +
  # Recession band (Feb–Apr 2020)
  geom_rect(
    data = recess_shade,
    aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year",
    date_labels = "%Y"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1.5, 2), breaks = seq(-1.5, 2, by = 0.5)) +  # ⬅ widen y-axis
  geom_line(color = col_orange, size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, color = "black") +
  labs(
    title    = "Treasury Spread (T10Y2Y)",
    subtitle = "10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Minus 2-Year Treasury Constant Maturity",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Percentage Points",
    caption  = "Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, shaded area = COVID recession (NBER)"   # ✅ citation added
  ) +
  theme_fred()

#{r Drates}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# 1. Pull the data
cc_delin <- fredr(
  series_id         = "DRCCLACBS",
  observation_start = as.Date("2019-01-01"),  # adjust as needed
  observation_end   = Sys.Date()
)

# 2. Create a label column with actual Qn YYYY format
cc_delin <- cc_delin %>%
  mutate(
    quarter_label = paste0("Q", quarter(date), " ", year(date))
  )



#{r Drates}
# 3 ── (Optional) recession shading for 2020 COVID downturn  
recess_shade <- data.frame(
  start = as.Date("2020-02-01"),   # NBER recession: Feb-2020
  end   = as.Date("2020-04-30")    #             …  Apr-2020
)


#{r Drates}
library(ggplot2)
keep <- quarter(cc_delin$date) %in% c(1, 3)
ggplot(cc_delin, aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  # Recession band (Feb–Apr 2020)
  geom_rect(
    data = recess_shade,
    aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(color = col_orange, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 2) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = cc_delin$date[keep],
    labels = cc_delin$quarter_label[keep]
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delinquency Rate on Credit-Card Loans - All Commercial Banks",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Percent - Quarterly Data",
    caption  = "Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, shaded area = COVID recession (NBER)"  # ✅ FRED series ID for credit card delinquency
  ) +
  theme_fred() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))



#{r Drates}
library(fredr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# 1 ── Download the series
biz_delin <- fredr(
  series_id         = "DRBLACBS",
  observation_start = as.Date("2019-10-01"),   # Q4-2019 to present
  observation_end   = Sys.Date()
)


#{r Drates}
# 2 ── Build custom quarter labels
biz_delin <- biz_delin %>%
  mutate(quarter_lbl = paste0("Q", quarter(date), " ", year(date)))


#{r Drates}
# 3 ── (Optional) recession shading for 2020 COVID downturn  
recess_shade <- data.frame(
  start = as.Date("2020-02-01"),   # NBER recession: Feb-2020
  end   = as.Date("2020-04-30")    #             …  Apr-2020
)


#{r Drates}
ggplot(biz_delin, aes(date, value)) +
  # Recession band (Feb–Apr 2020)
  geom_rect(
    data = recess_shade,
    aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  # Delinquency line and points
  geom_line(color = col_orange, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = col_orange, size = 2) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = biz_delin$date,
    labels = biz_delin$quarter_lbl
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delinquency Rate on Business Loans – All Commercial Banks",
    subtitle = "Quarterly Observations with 2020 Recession Shading",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Percent",
    caption  = fred_caption("DRBLACBS")  # ✅Source citation
  ) +
  theme_fred() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

#{r housing inventory}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(fredr)

# 1. Set your date window
start_date <- as.Date("2021-01-01")
end_date   <- Sys.Date()

# 2. Pull the three series
fitted_yield   <- fredr("THREEFY10", observation_start = start_date, observation_end = end_date)
forward_rate   <- fredr("THREEFF10", observation_start = start_date, observation_end = end_date)
term_premium   <- fredr("THREEFYTP10", observation_start = start_date, observation_end = end_date)

# 3. Combine into one tidy data frame
df <- tibble(
  date = fitted_yield$date,
  `10-year zero-coupon yield`           = fitted_yield$value,
  `Avg. exp. short rate next 10 years`  = forward_rate$value,
  `10-year zero-coupon term premium`    = term_premium$value
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "Component", values_to = "Value")

# 4. Plot
ggplot(df, aes(x = date, y = Value, color = Component)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, color = "black") +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "10-year zero-coupon yield"           = "#1f77b4",
    "Avg. exp. short rate next 10 years"  = "#2ca02c",
    "10-year zero-coupon term premium"    = "#d62728"
  )) +
  labs(
    title    = "Decomposition of Treasury Yields - ACM Model",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Percent",
    caption = "Source: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco"
  ) +
  theme_fred() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.title = element_blank())
